newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Incitec studying ammonium nitrate expansion.
newsitem.headline: Incitec studying ammonium nitrate expansion.

text.p: Chemicals and fertiliser group Incitec Ltd said it was well advanced on a feasibility study on expanding ammonium nitrate production at its manufacturing complex at Kooragang Island, Newcastle, New South Wales.
Managing director Jim Babon said the project, to cost about A$40 million, would result in a 100,000 tonne or 35 percent expansion in ammonium nitrate production capacity.
"With this expansion, and other investments at Kooragang Island over the last two years, we will have a world scale operation, producing 380,000 tonnes annually," he said in a statement.

"This is a substantial increase on the previous production capacity of 280,000 tonnes, and much of the increased output will support the explosives requirements of expanding coal production of the Hunter Region," Babon said.
Final approval of the ammonium nitrate project is scheduled for later this year, with commissioning in 1999, he said.
ICI Australia Ltd holds a 72 percent interest in Incitec.
